compatibility.intro: The 224DT 2.2 Duratorq was introduced to replace the PSA-sourced engines in the facelifted Freelander 2 and was carried over into the early Range Rover Evoque models before the Ingenium diesel takeover, serving as the core compact SUV diesel for Land Rover during this era.

costGuide.title: Land Rover 224DT Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 224DT typically takes 10-14 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a 224DT engine replacement is the condition of the EGR system and the turbocharger assembly. Units where the EGR cooler has been preemptively replaced and the turbo actuator serviced command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a Ford-sourced Duratorq unit, parts availability is excellent, keeping reconditioned 224DT prices competitive compared to proprietary JLR engines. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Land Rover 224DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: EGR Cooler Leaks and Valve Sticking
items.whatHappens: The EGR cooler can develop internal cracks, leading to coolant loss into the exhaust or intake. Additionally, the EGR valve itself can stick open due to carbon buildup, causing rough running, loss of power, and excessive smoke.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the EGR cooler and valve is a standard and relatively inexpensive repair. If coolant ingestion has caused hydro-locking or bearing damage, a full 224DT engine replacement is necessary.

items.title: Turbo Actuator and Seal Failure
items.whatHappens: The turbocharger wastegate actuator is prone to seizing or failing, leading to over-boosting or under-boosting. Turbo oil seals can also fail, allowing oil into the intake or exhaust manifolds.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the actuator or servicing the turbo is a relatively inexpensive fix. If the turbo has suffered catastrophic shaft failure and sent metal debris into the sump, a full 224DT engine replacement is often the only viable solution.

items.title: Injector Seal Leaks
items.whatHappens: The copper injector seat washers and O-rings degrade over time, allowing combustion gases and soot to build up around the injector base (often called "chuffing"). This leads to hard starting, misfires, and potential cylinder head damage if ignored.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the copper washers and seals is a routine and highly effective repair. If left ignored and cylinder head warping occurs, a full unit replacement is required.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 224DT is a Ford-sourced Duratorq engine, widely regarded as more robust than the preceding PSA units, but proactive EGR and turbo maintenance remains the critical factor in its long-term longevity .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 224DT
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the dipstick tube or on the transmission bell housing mating surface, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The 224DT is frequently confused with the PSA-sourced 2.2 TD4 (DW12) found in earlier Freelander 2 models, or the later Ingenium Land Rover 204DTD. Fitting a 204DTD into a 224DT vehicle requires extensive ECU remapping, different engine mounts, and altered cooling architecture, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 224DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 224DT is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof that the EGR cooler and turbo actuator have been recently serviced. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a failing EGR system or a starved turbo is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used 224DT engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 224DT addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include a refreshed EGR cooler and valve, a serviced turbocharger actuator, and new injector copper washers. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a Freelander 2 or Evoque without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned 224DT options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing signs of bore wear, or if the engine has already suffered turbo debris ingestion. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the fuel system to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom 224DT rebuild

items.question: What is the most common failure on the 224DT?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the 224DT are EGR cooler leaks, turbo actuator failure, and injector seal degradation. The EGR cooler can crack internally, leading to rapid coolant loss and potential hydro-locking. The turbo wastegate actuator is prone to seizing, causing over-boosting or under-boosting. Injector copper washers degrade over time, allowing combustion gas blow-by (chuffing) and hard starting.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 224DT engine?
items.answer: The 2.2L 224DT Duratorq was fitted to the Land Rover Freelander 2 (L359) and the early Range Rover Evoque (L538) from 2011 onwards. It replaced the older PSA-sourced 2.2 TD4 to meet stricter Euro 5 emissions standards. It is mechanically distinct from the later 2.0-litre Ingenium diesel (204DTD) that eventually succeeded it. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 224DT engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 224DT is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known age-related weaknesses of the EGR system and turbocharger. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting a cracked EGR cooler or a failing turbo actuator. Proper reconditioning proactively upgrades these specific weak points with refreshed components and new injector seals. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 224DT and not the older 2.2 TD4 or newer 2.0 Ingenium?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the dipstick tube. The 224DT is visually identifiable by its specific Ford Duratorq common-rail injection pump and turbo plumbing. It is commonly confused with the older PSA 2.2 TD4 or the newer 2.0 Ingenium (204DTD), which have entirely different cylinder heads and ECU mapping. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe compatibility and mapping issues.
